items.title: Chennai Dalit man hacked to death for falling in love, demand for anti-honour killing law rises
items.summary: A 23-year-old Dalit man was brutally hacked to death in yet another ‘honour’ killing in Tamil Nadu. Praveen Kumar, who was attacked with machetes on the night of August 16, succumbed to his injuries on August 20 at the Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital (RGGH) in Chennai. Praveen, who belonged to a Scheduled Caste community, was a resident of Kelambakkam in Chengalpattu district, very near to Chennai. Kelambakkam T-19 police have identified the perpetrators as Manikandan, Ezhumalai, Nantheesh, and Gautham. All four were arrested and sent to judicial custody on August 17. A search is underway for a fifth accused who is absconding, police also said. Ezhumalai is a member of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), according to multiple news reports, triggering further anger among anti-caste activists. Allegedly, Praveen and Ezhumalai’s daughter, Ashwathi, had been romantically interested in each other. Not the first instance of violence According to Sathish Kumar, a neighbour, both Praveen and Ezhumalai are from the Scheduled Caste (SC) Adi Dravidar community. items.title: BJP promises ‘positive content’. Its new social media team’s record tells another story
items.summary: Days after taking charge as the BJP’s national social media convenor, Deepak Mhaske told a gathering of reporters, “My focus will be to tackle the fake narrative spread by the Opposition, which uses AI in reels to twist facts and mislead people. We have been creating positive content and taking it to people. I will try to add momentum to this.” The 58-year-old chemistry professor-turned-politician has spent over a decade in the party’s IT cell. While he accused the Opposition of peddling “fake narratives” and promised to fight them with “positive content”, his own state unit’s Instagram account was busy dividing Gen Z into communal categories. Three weeks before his appointment, the BJP’s Chhattisgarh unit posted a reel juxtaposing an Instagram creator’s video from a Mumbai protest against NEET-UG paper leaks with footage of a student receiving an award from President Droupadi Murmu. It described the creator as “ Babar ki virasat par thumke lagane waale Gen-Z ” and the student as “ Chhattisgarh ke maan badhane wale Gen-Z ”. items.title: The judge who made room for the young
items.summary: There are judges whose legacy is measured in landmark judgments they had delivered while in office and there are judges whose contribution is remembered through constitutional principles that continue to shape the law long after they have left the bench. And then there are judges whose legacy lies in something less visible, but perhaps equally important in terms of the people they encouraged, the confidence they instilled in others and the opportunities they created. Justice Sanjay Karol , who retires from the Supreme Court today, belongs to that last category in a way that deserves to be remembered. I say this not merely as an observer of the Court, but as someone who had the opportunity, in the early days of my clerkship (July to September 2025) at the Supreme Court, to sit in his courtroom. The judge under whom I am clerking was bench partner with Justice Karol during the relevant time. What stayed with me from his Court was not one particular judgment or one particular exchange. Rather, it was the atmosphere of the courtroom itself. It was a young lawyer’s courtroom. items.title: 11th HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition: LIVE UPDATES
items.summary: National Law University (NLU) Delhi will be hosting the 11th edition of the HSF Kramer-NLU Delhi International Negotiation Competition (INC) beginning today. Organised jointly by Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer (HSF Kramer) and NLU Delhi, the competition has been held since 2014. This year's edition runs from August 21 to 23 at the University's campus in Sector-14, Dwarka. 38 teams from law schools around the world are expected to take part. Each university fields one team of two students. Participants will step into the roles of international lawyers, negotiating a series of legal problems modelled on real-life situations. Each round will be judged by a panel that includes renowned lawyers and academicians. The competition consists of two preliminary rounds followed by knock-out advanced rounds. The two advanced-round winners will then face off in the final. Today's proceedings begin at 3 PM with registration and penalty appeals of Negotiation Plans for Preliminary Rounds, followed by the inaugural ceremony, opening ceremony, and a panel discussion titled Practitioners' Masterclass on M&A. Speaking to ANI , Mishra dismissed Reddy’s letter as being part of a political vendetta, and also disputed references to Reddy as a BCI co-chairman. Mishra claimed that Reddy is not the co-chairman of BCI. " First of all, I must clarify that he is not a co-chairman of the Bar Council of India. Therefore, he is no more even a member of the State Bar Council of Karnataka," Mishra said. It may be noted that the BCI’s web page for its office bearers shows Reddy as a co-chairman at the time of writing this article. Earlier, Chief Minister Joseph Vijay had announced in the Assembly that all the legislators would receive a car and Rs 75,000 monthly vehicle allowance for constituency-related work. Udhayanidhi said, “DMK members do not need government cars. Cars should be given to those who are struggling, taking into account the state's economic situation.
